fixes.explanation: YES, baker! Pay back the value AND a fifth on top. That's not a refund, that's a refund with a little extra tucked in the box. The text says he makes restitution by "…adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest…" (Leviticus 5:16). And the same verse says that priest makes atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering.

Elders sound so official, friend, like the one person at the front desk who looks the most in charge. I'd have handed it to them too, with a nervous smile. But the verse says he gives it "…to the priest, who will make atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering…" (Leviticus 5:16). No elders in that verse at all.

Ooh, the Levites didn't make the guest list on this one, friend. This verse has exactly one name for the payment, and it's not them. He gives the value plus a fifth "…to the priest…" (Leviticus 5:16). Same priest who makes atonement with the ram, so he's handling the whole thing, start to finish.

Fair guess, friend. The priest is busy in this passage, that man has rams to handle. But when the verse names who the unfaithfulness is against, it doesn't say him. It says the man "…acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor…" (Leviticus 6:2). The LORD's own words, right there.
